nodes.label: MSK.GetVehicleFromPlate
nodes.rationale: The existing MSK.GetVehicleWithPlate and MSK.GetClosestVehicleWithPlate both need a point and a radius, so a plate alone could not find a vehicle. The lookup always runs server side so no client walks its own vehicle pool and the answer covers every vehicle on the server, not only streamed-in ones. Cost of that choice: the client call is a blocking callback round trip and must run inside a thread. A network id without a local handle is a valid result meaning the vehicle is not streamed in for that client.

nodes.label: MSK.GetModelFromPlate
nodes.rationale: Reads the framework's vehicle table (owned_vehicles on ESX, player_vehicles with vehicle+hash on QBCore) rather than the world, so it still answers while the vehicle is parked in a garage and does not exist as an entity. Blocking on client and server, so it must be called from a thread. Other frameworks return nil.

nodes.label: Plate Trim and Upper Case Normalization
nodes.rationale: GTA returns plates space padded while plates from a database, command or config are usually trimmed and not necessarily upper case, so comparisons never matched. Both sides of every comparison are now trimmed and upper cased. Inner spaces are deliberately kept, so AB C123 and ABC123 remain distinct plates. Scoped to the two new functions only, the older ...WithPlate functions are unchanged to avoid behavior drift.
nodes.norm_label: plate trim and upper case normalization

nodes.label: Per-Component NUI Error Boundary
nodes.rationale: A single throw in one component previously unmounted the whole interface, taking notify, input, numpad, progressbar, textui and both menus down together until the resource restarted. Wrapping each component isolates the blast radius. A failed component logs its name and stack to the client console instead of vanishing silently and recovers on the next NUI message.

nodes.label: Three Failures in Thirty Seconds Crash Loop Rule
nodes.rationale: Only three failures within thirty seconds count as a crash loop and keep the component hidden until restart. The threshold exists so a rare bad call degrades gracefully and does not disable a component for the whole session, while a genuinely broken component stops thrashing.
nodes.norm_label: three failures in thirty seconds crash loop rule

nodes.label: Color Code Parser nil Text Handling
nodes.rationale: The parser called String.slice on whatever it received, so one call with a nil text (for example MSK.Notification('some text') with the message parameter omitted) threw inside React and, absent an error boundary, unmounted the entire NUI. It now returns an empty result for nil and coerces numbers to strings, so a bad call degrades to an empty label instead of killing the interface.
nodes.norm_label: color code parser nil text handling

nodes.label: Context Menu (mouse driven)
nodes.rationale: Registered once under an id and reopened as often as needed. Options carry icons, descriptions, images, progress bars, hover metadata, disabled and readOnly rows, and can run onSelect, fire event/serverEvent, or drill into another registered menu. It deliberately takes NUI mouse focus (so the player stands still) because clicking requires the mouse.

nodes.label: Menu (keyboard navigated NativeUI style list)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately does not take NUI focus: arrow keys are read through game controls and only the navigation controls are disabled, so the player can keep walking and driving while the menu is on screen. The full state (selected row, current values, checkbox states) lives in Lua so onSelected, onSideScroll, onCheck and onClose always receive authoritative values rather than trusting the NUI.

nodes.label: Live Menu Updates (UpdateContext / UpdateMenu)
nodes.rationale: Addresses a single option through its id and merges only the changed fields, refreshing the UI live when that menu is open. Removes the need to rebuild and reopen an entire menu just to move a progress bar, relabel a row or disable an option.

nodes.label: Namespaced Menu API (MSK.Context.* / MSK.Menu.*)
nodes.rationale: Aligns both menus with the rest of the library where MSK.Input.Open and MSK.Cron.Create already use namespaces. Nothing breaks: the flat v3.1.0 names (MSK.RegisterContext, MSK.ShowMenu, ...) alias the same functions and exports are unchanged. MSK.Menu.Hide replaces MSK.Menu.Close for symmetry with MSK.Context.Hide, with Close kept as an alias.

nodes.label: Menu Internal Navigation Leak Fix
nodes.rationale: MSK.Menu.Move, SideScroll and Select appeared on the public table but were only reachable inside msk_core, so consumer resources calling them failed. They were made module-internal instead of being exported, keeping the public surface honest.

nodes.label: Shared Registration Guard for Eager Loaded Modules
nodes.rationale: Several modules registered msk_core owned listeners (net events, callbacks, commands, background threads) unconditionally, so eager loading a module in a consumer fxmanifest started a second copy that interfered server wide: duplicate notifications, doubled death and vehicle events, twice-enforced bans, doubled cron ticks, and callbacks re-registered with closures that broke when the consumer stopped. Shared registrations are now guarded to run only inside msk_core while consumers keep the full callable API through the export proxy, making every module safe to eager load.
nodes.norm_label: shared registration guard for eager loaded modules

nodes.label: Cron Module Return Value Fix
nodes.rationale: The Cron module returned true, which the consumer loader cached over the MSK.Cron table, so only MSK.CreateCron and MSK.DeleteCron stayed reachable. Returning the MSK.Cron table restores MSK.Cron.Create and MSK.Cron.Delete as documented.

nodes.label: QBCore Item Functions Wrapper Fix
nodes.rationale: The QBCore player wrapper read item helpers from self.PlayerData.Functions, which is nil because QBCore exposes them on Player.Functions, so AddItem/RemoveItem/HasItem/GetItem crashed MSK.GetPlayer() consumers with 'attempt to index a nil value (field Functions)'. They now read self.Functions, consistent with the rest of the wrapper.

nodes.label: Auto Release Workflow from CHANGELOGS.md
nodes.rationale: CI (CodeQL for the NUI, a NUI build check), Dependabot for npm and GitHub Actions, and a workflow that tags and publishes a release from the matching CHANGELOGS.md section. These files live in the repository only and are not part of the resource uploaded to a server, so the release artifact stays clean.

nodes.label: NUI Rebuild on React 19 / Vite 8 / TypeScript 7
nodes.rationale: Pure dependency bump with no API or behavior change, the Lua side untouched. FontAwesome 7 ships only woff2, so the unused .ttf font files were dropped from web/dist to shrink the shipped resource.
nodes.norm_label: nui rebuild on react 19 / vite 8 / typescript 7

nodes.label: Framework Bridge (ESX / QBCore / ox_core / STANDALONE)
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: Write once, run on any supported framework. Detection is automatic via Config.Framework = 'AUTO', so consumer resources never branch on framework themselves.

nodes.label: Inventory Bridge
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: Abstracts ox_inventory, core_inventory, jaksam_inventory, the ESX/Chezza default, or a custom adapter behind one API so item calls stay identical across servers.

nodes.label: Lazy Loaded Modules
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: A module is compiled into the consumer resource only on first use, so a resource pays only for what it touches.

nodes.label: Eager Loading via msk_core '<Module>'
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: Opt-out of lazy loading by listing a module in the consumer fxmanifest so it is compiled up front instead of on first call.

nodes.label: Dual API (MSK table and exports.msk_core)
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: Every function is reachable both as MSK.Function(...) for resources that import import.lua and as exports.msk_core:Function(...) for those that do not, so the core is usable without the shared_script import.

nodes.label: @msk_core/import.lua Shared Script
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: One line in a consumer fxmanifest exposes the global MSK table everywhere in that resource. Requires lua54 'yes' in every importing resource.

nodes.label: React + Vite + TypeScript NUI
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: Notify, Input, Numpad, Progressbar and TextUI, fully offline and bundled. The built web/dist is committed to the repository so the game server never needs npm; only development requires npm run dev / npm run build.

nodes.label: oxmysql Requirement
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: The only hard dependency. Frameworks and inventories are optional and only gate the framework- or inventory-based functions.

nodes.label: Resource Start Order Constraint
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: msk_core must start after the framework and inventory it bridges and before any resource that consumes it, otherwise auto-detection has nothing to detect and consumers import an unready core.

nodes.label: LGPL-3.0-or-later Licensing
nodes.author: MSK Scripts | Musiker15
nodes.rationale: LGPL was chosen over GPL so the core itself stays open while any resource, free or paid, may depend on msk_core without being forced to adopt the same license. The MSK Scripts and Musiker15 names, logos and brands are trademarks and explicitly outside the LGPL grant.
